name: opencode
notes: TypeScript/Bun AI coding agent monorepo. Core runtime lives in packages/opencode/src with client/server architecture, OpenAPI 3.1, SSE, agent profiles (build/plan/general/explore), session compaction, plugin and MCP tool dispatch, and SQLite-backed persistence. Study packages/opencode/src for provider wiring, session loop, permissions, and built-in tools.

name: cline
notes: VS Code-first TypeScript coding agent; repo/product name is Cline, published package name is claude-dev. For brain-server integration, start with src/core/api/providers/openai.ts and src/core/api/index.ts for OpenAI-compatible backend wiring, webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/OpenAICompatible.tsx for base URL + model config UI, docs/provider-config/openai-compatible.mdx for expected setup, and src/standalone plus src/hosts/external for non-VS Code host paths.

name: openclaw
notes: TypeScript personal AI assistant (312K+ stars). Multi-platform channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, etc.). Voice/audio support. Study for channel abstraction, plugin/tool system, session architecture, multi-platform patterns.

name: zeroclaw
notes: PRIMARY REFERENCE. Rust AI agent (26K+ stars). Trait-driven architecture, 3.4MB binary, <5MB RAM. Swappable providers/channels/tools via traits (not plugins). SQLite + hybrid keyword/vector memory. 22+ model providers. Security: gateway pairing, sandboxing, fs scoping. Study for trait design, provider abstraction, tool system, memory architecture.

name: ironclaw
notes: Rust AI agent framework (~25K lines, 432+ tests). Security-first: 13-step security pipeline, zero-trust, WASM sandboxing, encrypted vault for API keys. 25+ LLM providers, 20+ channels. Study for security patterns, WASM sandboxing, permission validation, provider presets.

name: oh-my-pi
notes: TypeScript/Rust monorepo AI coding agent (1.9K stars). Layered packages: pi-ai (LLM comms), pi-agent-core (agent loop), pi-coding-agent (full runtime + sessions), pi-tui (terminal UI). Study for agent loop layering, RPC protocol (packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md), session compaction, tool system, conventional commit generation.

name: pi-mono
notes: TypeScript monorepo AI agent toolkit. Includes pi-ai (provider abstraction), pi-agent-core (runtime), pi-coding-agent (coding agent CLI), pi-tui, pi-web-ui, pi-pods, and Slack bot tooling. Study for package layering, unified provider API, agent runtime boundaries, coding-agent tool execution, and terminal/web UI integration.

name: vercel-ai
notes: Vercel AI SDK (22K+ stars). TypeScript toolkit for AI apps. Study for unified provider abstraction (switch providers by changing one line), streaming protocol, tool calling interface, structured output with type-safe schemas. Multi-framework (Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Node). packages/ai-sdk-core is the key package.

name: agent-browser
notes: Vercel Labs browser automation CLI for AI agents. Pin matches the locally installed CLI version. Start with cli/src for the Rust command/runtime implementation; use skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md for the upstream coding-agent workflow, README.md for the full CLI surface, bin/agent-browser.js for the JS launcher wrapper, and docs/src when researching auth, sessions, dashboard, or provider-specific behavior.

name: openai-node
notes: Official OpenAI Node SDK. Use root api.md for the documented SDK surface, then inspect src/resources/responses and related generated request/streaming types for concrete create-response request fields and event coverage. Treat this as a validation source for the Responses API surface, not a replacement for the official docs when the SDK lags.

name: rig
notes: Rust LLM and agent SDK workspace. Core library lives in rig/rig-core/src with first-class provider abstractions, tool traits, agent loops, vector-store integrations, and app-focused building blocks. Study for provider/tool/RAG composition rather than a full coding-agent runtime.

name: async-openai
notes: Rust OpenAI client (688K downloads/month). Study for SSE streaming implementation, tool calling wire format, chat completion types, reqwest usage patterns. Will be used directly or as reference for brain-providers OpenAI implementation.

name: gastown
notes: Advanced Go-based multi-agent orchestration layer for Claude Code and compatible runtimes. Focus on persistent work tracking via git worktrees/hooks, mayor-style coordination, convoy workflow, agent identities, runtime abstraction for Claude/Codex/Cursor/OpenCode/pi, dashboard/TUI surfaces, and orchestration concerns above a core engine.

name: attractor
notes: Graph-driven orchestration layer with companion specs for coding-agent loops and unified LLM clients. Start with coding-agent-loop-spec.md for provider-aligned tool contracts, especially OpenAI apply_patch in V4A format, then attractor-spec.md and unified-llm-spec.md for orchestration concerns similar to Gastown.

name: ouroboros
notes: Python self-modifying agent PoC. Original Colab/Telegram runtime with Git-backed self-editing, BIBLE.md constitution, background consciousness loop, persistent identity/scratchpad memory, task decomposition, multi-model review, and supervisor-managed workers. Study as a concrete prototype for agent self-rewrite and continuity, not as a finished distributed autonomy platform. README also points to a newer desktop successor under joi-lab/ouroboros-desktop.

name: ouroboros-desktop
notes: Desktop successor to the original Ouroboros runtime. Native app with PyWebView launcher, Starlette server, web UI, local-model support, dual-layer safety, and a stronger immutable-shell plus self-editable-core split. Study for the evolution from Telegram/Colab PoC toward a more durable sovereign runtime.

name: evoagentx
notes: Python framework for building, evaluating, and evolving agentic workflows. Strong adjacent reference for workflow generation, automated evaluation, memory modules, tool-rich multi-agent pipelines, and explicit self-evolution algorithms. Useful as a concept cousin to Ouroboros rather than a direct lineage match.

name: llama_cpp-rs
notes: DEPRECATED for our use. High-level async Rust bindings to llama.cpp but stuck at v0.3.2 (April 2024). Does NOT support Qwen3.5 GATED_DELTA_NET. Kept for reference only.

name: llama-cpp-2
notes: ACTIVELY MAINTAINED Rust bindings to llama.cpp (v0.1.138, March 2026). 309K downloads. Lower-level than edgenai but much more current. Wraps llama.cpp with GATED_DELTA_NET support for Qwen3.5. Key types: LlamaModel, LlamaContext (session). Features: CUDA, Metal, Vulkan. Used as the basis for LlamaCppProvider.

name: mistral.rs
notes: Rust inference engine for LLMs. Supports GGUF, ISQ, and multiple architectures. Used by brain-providers MistralRsProvider. Study for GgufModelBuilder API, stream_chat_request, Model type, TextMessages. Does NOT support Qwen3.5 Gated DeltaNet architecture as of v0.7.

name: axum
notes: Tokio-native HTTP framework (20K+ stars). Built on Tower/hyper. Built-in SSE support via axum::response::sse. Used for brain-server network mode (REST + SSE). Key modules: routing, extract, response (including sse), middleware.

name: agent-client-protocol
notes: Official Rust SDK for Agent Client Protocol (ACP). JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio. Provides Agent and Client traits. Used by Zed editor. v0.10.2 (March 2026). brain implements the Agent trait to be accessible from any ACP-compatible editor. Key: examples/agent.rs for reference implementation.

name: agent-client-protocol-spec
notes: Canonical ACP protocol/spec repository. Includes transport docs, lifecycle docs, schema, and RFDs. Use for protocol surface, Streamable HTTP status, session semantics, and extension points rather than SDK implementation details.

name: @zed-industries/codex-acp
notes: ACP-compatible Codex adapter published by Zed Industries. Use for how a production ACP wrapper maps Codex CLI/runtime behavior into ACP sessions, prompts, approvals, and editor-facing capabilities.

name: zed
notes: Zed editor source. Use to verify the external agent / ACP client transport implementation and the concrete behavior behind agent_servers, registry installs, and ACP session launch paths.

name: vscode-acp
notes: VS Code ACP client extension. Use to assess whether VS Code currently has a credible generic ACP chat/editor client and what ACP features it expects from agents.

name: acpx
notes: Headless CLI client for the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). Use for terminal-side ACP session lifecycle, queueing, permissions, structured output, built-in Codex adapter behavior, and custom ACP server launch flows via --agent.

name: forge
notes: OpenTUI/Solid terminal UI for ACP agents. Start with packages/forge/src/acp for the ACP client/orchestrator, packages/forge/src/cli/cmd/tui for the terminal UI, and packages/forge/test/acp for real protocol coverage. Key question for brain: Forge is a real ACP-native TUI, but agent launch currently appears registry-driven rather than a documented raw custom-command path.

name: nori-cli
notes: Rust/Ratatui terminal AI client forked from Codex CLI with ACP-native subprocess orchestration. Start with codex-rs/acp for the ACP registry, connection, event translation, and custom-agent config path; codex-rs/tui for the terminal UX; and codex-rs/tui-pty-e2e/tests for real ACP session, file, approval, and custom-agent coverage. Important question for brain: Nori now appears to support custom ACP agents via [[agents]] in config.toml rather than only built-in Claude/Codex/Gemini providers.

name: acp-ui
notes: Tauri/Vue desktop ACP client with explicit custom agent command configuration. Start with src/lib/acp-bridge.ts and src/stores/session.ts for ACP method coverage and update handling, plus src-tauri/src/agent.rs and src-tauri/src/config.rs for subprocess launch, agents.json config, and hot reload. Important question for brain: acp-ui looks strong for custom-command launch and file/permission flows, but may intentionally expose a smaller ACP client capability surface than richer TUIs.

name: agentic.nvim
notes: Neovim ACP-first client/plugin. Use to inspect how a keyboard-first editor shell launches ACP agents, restores sessions, renders streaming chat and diffs, and exposes ACP-native debug and provider configuration for custom servers such as brain acp.

name: codecompanion.nvim
notes: Broad Neovim AI framework with ACP support among many adapters. Use to compare how much ACP sits at the center of the UX versus being one backend inside a richer chat/workflow platform, and to study custom agent launch, session handling, tools, and approval surfaces.

name: ratatui
notes: Leading Rust TUI library (19K+ stars). Immediate-mode rendering with crossterm/termion/termwiz backends. Built-in widgets: Paragraph, List, Table, Block, Scrollbar, Gauge, Tabs. Study for layout system (Constraint, Layout, Rect), widget trait, Frame/Buffer rendering, styling, and the app loop pattern. Key dependency for brain-cli TUI.

name: tui-textarea
notes: Multiline text editor widget for ratatui (489 stars). Emacs keybindings, undo/redo, search, selection, line numbers, yank, mouse scroll. Used as input widget for brain-cli TUI prompt. Also see ratatui-textarea (community fork, v0.8.0).

name: codex
notes: OpenAI Codex CLI (65K+ stars). Dual-stack: codex-cli (TypeScript/Node) is the original CLI, codex-rs (Rust) is the rewrite. Lightweight coding agent running in terminal. Study for Rust agent architecture, provider wiring, tool system, sandboxing, session persistence, config layout, and storage patterns.

name: schemars
notes: Rust JSON Schema generation crate. Use for derive behavior, doc-comment-to-description/title mapping, schema attributes, and serde interaction when generating tool request/response schemas for agent-tools.

name: models.dev
notes: Open-source AI model database (3K+ stars). TOML-based model specs organized by provider in providers/<name>/models/<id>.toml. Schema: name, family, reasoning (bool), tool_call, attachment, structured_output, temperature, knowledge, release_date, cost (input/output/reasoning/cache_read/cache_write), limit (context/input/output), modalities, status. Used as canonical data source for brain ModelInfo presets.

name: terminal-bench
notes: Official Terminal-Bench repository. Start with terminal_bench/ for the benchmark runtime, agents, parsers, terminal orchestration, and registry client. adapters/ contains dataset adapters and docker/ contains MCP/server and container setup.

name: harbor
notes: Harbor evaluation framework. Start with src/harbor for the core framework and adapters/ for dataset-specific integrations and parity experiments. Useful for registry clients, trajectories, trial orchestration, and benchmark adapters.

name: KIRA
notes: KRAFTON AI benchmark and product repo. Start with terminus_kira/ for the Terminus-KIRA Terminal-Bench harness redesign on top of Terminus 2. Also inspect KiraClaw/docs for the broader second-iteration runtime and product architecture, especially the move toward an embedded long-running agent daemon rather than a benchmark-only harness.

name: swe-bench
notes: Official SWE-bench repository. Start with swebench/harness for evaluation logic, swebench/inference for run entrypoints, and swebench/resources for packaged task assets and environment definitions.

name: mini-swe-agent
notes: Minimal SWE-agent scaffold focused on reproducible, explicit agent workflows for SWE-bench-style tasks. Start with run/, agents/, models/, and config/benchmarks for the concrete scaffold assumptions.

name: hal-harness
notes: HAL evaluation harness from Princeton PLI. Start with hal/benchmarks, hal/benchmark_manager.py, hal/agent_runner.py, and agents/ for example agent integrations across supported benchmark families.

name: osworld
notes: Official OSWorld repository. Start with desktop_env/ for the environment and evaluator implementation, then mm_agents/ for agent-side integrations and evaluation_examples/ for runnable examples.

name: visualwebarena
notes: Official VisualWebArena repository. Start with evaluation_harness/ for scoring and task execution, browser_env/ for environment logic, and agent/ for prompt and policy setup.

name: appworld
notes: Official AppWorld repository. Start with src/appworld for the environment, evaluator, and APIs; experiments/ contains prompts and benchmark-oriented experiment code.

name: openhands-benchmarks
notes: OpenHands benchmark evaluation repository. Start with benchmarks/ for active suites including swebench and terminalbench; vendor/ and the README document how the repo ties into the Software Agent SDK.

name: openhands-software-agent-sdk
notes: OpenHands Software Agent SDK. Start with openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk for conversation, tool, event, critic, and subagent runtime code; pair with the benchmarks repo to understand newer OpenHands evaluation flows.

name: @anthropic-ai/sdk
notes: Official Anthropic TypeScript SDK. Use for Messages request/response types, SSE event shapes, tool-use blocks, and general API behavior when implementing provider-anthropic.

name: letta-code
notes: Memory-first TypeScript coding harness built on Letta agents. Use as a contrast point for persistent agent memory, long-lived agent identity across sessions, and the distinction between stateful agent architecture and loop-language power.

name: utoipa
notes: Rust OpenAPI generation library. For axum integration, start with utoipa-axum/src plus examples/todo-axum/src and examples/simple-axum/src. Core schema/derive behavior lives in utoipa/src and utoipa-gen/src. Research for generated /doc on axum-based agent-server compat routes, especially handler annotations, schema derives, path/query/body typing, and how route inventory stays aligned with the generated spec.

name: aide
notes: Rust code-first API documentation library with Axum integration. Start with crates/aide/src/axum plus examples/example-axum/src for the concrete router/documentation flow; macros live in crates/aide-macros/src. Research ApiRouter/api_route ergonomics, schema extraction via schemars, operation metadata, and whether docs and route registration can share one source of truth for agent-server compat.

name: hono-openapi
notes: OpenCode 1.3.2 route-to-OpenAPI bridge. Start with src for describeRoute, resolver, validator, openAPIRouteHandler, and generateSpecs. Compare its route-local contract model to agent-server's aide-based generation.

name: @standard-community/standard-openapi
notes: OpenCode 1.3.2 downstream OpenAPI conversion library. Start with src and compare its JSON Schema to OpenAPI conversion behavior against the local patched copy in repocache/anomalyco/opencode/patches.

name: @standard-community/standard-json
notes: Standard Schema to JSON Schema conversion library used under OpenCode's OpenAPI pipeline. Study the Zod and optional peer conversion path before blaming aide/schemars for every mismatch.

name: zod-to-json-schema
notes: Zod-to-JSON-Schema converter in the OpenCode 1.3.2 dependency graph. Use to understand how Zod-originating shapes may differ before standard-openapi emits the final OpenAPI document.
